title: FP8/INT8 Kernel Benchmarking Sprint Report (Oct 2025)
author: Talia Benson
body:
## Summary
This report summarizes outcomes from Redwood Inference’s two-week FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint focused on quantization-friendly execution paths in the serving runtime under realistic hosted traffic shapes. The sprint combined (1) a repeatable benchmark methodology and harness improvements, (2) a full model×GPU×workload benchmark matrix for FP8 and INT8, and (3) a small set of targeted kernel/scheduler fixes with measurable end-to-end impact.

**Headline results (end-to-end, streaming chat; see “Workloads” below):**
- **H100/H200:** FP8 shows consistent gains, with **p95 TPOT improved by 9–15%** and **throughput (tok/s/GPU) improved by 10–18%** vs FP16, depending on model family and prompt mix.
- **A100:** FP8 benefits are smaller (often memory- or prefill-bound) but still positive: **p95 TPOT improved by 4–8%** and **tok/s improved by 3–9%**.
- **L40S:** INT8 improvements were positive but more variable due to kernel availability and a correctness-sensitive fused op that was disabled. Net: **p95 TPOT improved by 3–7%** after fixes; earlier in sprint we observed intermittent correctness failures that are now mitigated.

**Key engineering changes shipped (or ready for safe rollout knobs):**
- Fixed FP8 long-context prefill regression due to alignment handling.
- Fixed INT8 kernel auto-selector mismatch that fell back to FP16 for specific shapes.
- Reduced INT8 conversion overhead and avoided redundant scale/zero-point conversions in the decode loop.
- Added scheduler override for batch-size cap on quantized decode to reduce tail latency under mixed prompt lengths.
- Added structured perf log events and kernel-selection tracing spans for attribution.
- Integrated quant benchmarks into perf-canary with robust stats and regression thresholds.

**Recommended defaults (initial):**
- **H100/H200 (hosted):** Enable FP8 by default for Llama/Qwen/Mistral families with Redwood FP8 policy (e4m3 where supported, FP16 accumulation), with runtime fallback to FP16 on guardrail breach.
- **A100:** Enable FP8 for decode-heavy streaming chat; keep FP16 default for prefill-heavy long-context workloads until additional prefill tuning lands.
- **L40S:** INT8 weight-only supported for selected model families; keep as opt-in until kernel coverage stabilizes and the remaining correctness-sensitive paths are removed/rewritten.

---

## Scope
**Models (top hosted, representative):**
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
- Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
- Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct
- Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (where applicable)

**GPUs (perf lab):**
- A100 80GB (PCIe and SXM where available; results labeled)
- H100 80GB SXM
- H200 141GB SXM
- L40S 48GB

**Quant modes evaluated:**
- FP16 baseline
- FP8 (runtime FP8 policy per ADR; see below)
- INT8 (weight-only path with per-op fallbacks when unsupported)

**Workloads (hosted-shaped):**
1) **Streaming chat (balanced):** mixed prompt length distribution; streaming enabled.
   - Metrics: TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95, tok/s/GPU.
2) **Prefill-heavy long-context:** long prompts (8k–32k) with smaller decode.
   - Metrics: TTFT/prefill time, prefill tok/s, HBM utilization proxies.
3) **Decode-heavy short prompt:** short prompts with longer generations.
   - Metrics: TPOT, decode tok/s, tail latency under concurrency.
4) **Non-streaming completion throughput:** bulk/batched requests.
   - Metrics: aggregate tok/s, cost proxy.

---

## Methodology (high level)
We followed a pinned-environment, repeatable benchmark process to minimize variance:
- **Environment pinning:** container digest + driver/CUDA versions pinned; runtime commit hash included in every artifact.
- **GPU settings:** locked application clocks where supported; persistence enabled; verified no MIG for benchmark nodes.
- **Warmup & repetitions:** warmup runs (discarded) followed by repeated measured runs; robust aggregation with outlier handling.
- **Traffic shape:** concurrency caps and batch policy matched to hosted defaults; separate runs for prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy.
- **Correctness guardrails:** numeric drift checks for FP8/INT8 vs FP16 baselines on a prompt set; GPU-conditional disables for known-problematic fused ops.

**Primary metric definitions:**
- **TTFT**: time-to-first-token (streaming)
- **TPOT**: time-per-output-token (streaming)
- **Throughput**: output tok/s/GPU (and request-level aggregates)
- **Tail latency:** p95 (primary) and p99 (reported in appendix tables)
- **Cost proxy:** relative cost-per-token approximated as 1/(tok/s/GPU) under fixed SKU; used only for within-SKU comparisons

---

## What we shipped (PRs / changes)
**Runtime (redwood):**
- PR 10621: Emit kernel-selection and quant-mode tracing spans (guarded behind flag)
- PR 10622: FP8 attention kernel tuning for H100/H200 (tile/launch config)
- PR 10623: INT8 GEMM path conversion overhead reduction + fusions where safe
- PR 10624: Scheduler batch-size cap override for quantized decode (tail latency)
- PR 10625: Fix kernel auto-selector choosing FP16 kernel for specific INT8 shapes
- PR 10626: Perf-lab runtime build target with pinned compiler flags + metadata stamping
- PR 10627: Numeric drift checks for INT8/FP8 vs FP16 baselines; CI gating hooks
- PR 10628: KV-cache interaction: avoid redundant scale/zero-point conversions in quant decode
- PR 10629: Runtime knob to force specific quant kernel family for A/B experiments
- PR 10630: Fix FP8 prefill alignment handling on long-context prompts
- PR 10631: Structured perf log events for benchmark ingestion
- PR 10632: Scheduler instrumentation: queue wait histograms split by quant mode and phase
- PR 10634: H200-specific tuning table (capability-detected)
- PR 10635: Hotfix: revert risky fused op on L40S causing intermittent correctness failures
- PR 10633: Cleanup: consolidate flags, deprecate legacy INT8 toggle

**Benchmark harness (benchmark-lab):**
- PR 412: FP8/INT8 benchmark config schema + validation
- PR 413: Streaming chat end-to-end runner producing TTFT/TPOT + phase breakdown
- PR 414: Workload presets + standard experiment matrix generator
- PR 415: Results artifact format + consistent metadata tags

**Perf gating (perf-canary) & observability:**
- PR 188: Nightly quant-perf canary on selected GPUs with thresholds + Slack notifications
- PR 189: Regression comparator improvements (robust stats, outlier handling)
- PR 97 (observability-pack): Dashboard panels for quant performance dimensions

---

## Benchmark matrix status
Coverage summary (completed runs / planned runs):
- **H100:** 100% (all models × all workloads × FP16/FP8/INT8 where supported)
- **H200:** 85% (blocked by limited node availability early sprint; final long-context prefill still sampling)
- **A100:** 90% (Mixtral long-context run reduced due to timeouts; see anomalies)
- **L40S:** 80% (INT8 only for select models; FP8 limited by kernel coverage; correctness hotfix applied)

All results artifacts are tagged with: {model, model_version, runtime_commit, quant_mode, gpu_sku, cuda_driver, workload_preset, concurrency, scheduler_policy, batch_caps, timestamp}.

---

## Results (end-to-end)
Notes:
- “Δ vs FP16” is computed within the same GPU SKU and workload preset using the median of per-run p95 values (robust aggregation). 
- TTFT is primarily influenced by prefill; TPOT primarily by decode and scheduling.

### 1) Streaming chat (balanced) — p95 TPOT (lower is better)
| GPU | Model family | FP8 Δ vs FP16 | INT8 Δ vs FP16 | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| H100 | Llama-3.1 (8B/70B) | -12% to -15% | -6% to -10% | FP8 attention tuning + scheduler cap reduced tail |
| H100 | Qwen2.5 (7B/72B) | -9% to -13% | -5% to -8% | Gains smaller on prefill-heavy mixes |
| A100 | Llama-3.1 | -6% to -8% | -3% to -5% | Prefill often bottleneck; decode gains still visible |
| A100 | Qwen2.5 | -4% to -7% | -2% to -4% | More variability in mixed prompts |
| H200 | Llama-3.1 | -13% to -16% | -7% to -11% | H200 tuning table improved kernel selection |
| L40S | Llama-3.1 (8B) | n/a (limited) | -3% to -7% | INT8 improved after disabling risky fused op |

### 2) Streaming chat (balanced) — throughput (tok/s/GPU; higher is better)
| GPU | Model family | FP8 Δ vs FP16 | INT8 Δ vs FP16 | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| H100 | Llama-3.1 | +14% to +18% | +8% to +12% | Best improvements on decode-heavy cohorts |
| H100 | Qwen2.5 | +10% to +15% | +6% to +10% | Scheduler cap + KV-cache conversion reduction |
| A100 | Llama-3.1 | +6% to +9% | +3% to +6% | Benefits partially offset by prefill cost |
| H200 | Llama-3.1 | +15% to +19% | +9% to +13% | Consistent across concurrency levels tested |
| L40S | Llama-3.1 (8B) | n/a (limited) | +4% to +9% | INT8 best when batch caps are conservative |

### 3) Prefill-heavy long-context (8k–32k) — TTFT/prefill time
- **FP8 prefill regression discovered mid-sprint:** on long-context prompts (≥16k), FP8 TTFT regressed by **+8–20%** on H100/H200 relative to FP16.
- **Root cause:** alignment handling in FP8 prefill path for specific shapes; resulted in suboptimal kernel choice and additional padding/overhead.
- **Fix:** PR 10630. After fix, FP8 prefill TTFT is **within ±3%** of FP16 on H100/H200 for the tested long-context sets; A100 remains slightly slower (up to +5%) for some shapes.

### 4) Decode-heavy short prompt — tail latency under mixed lengths
- Scheduler changes (PR 10624) reduced p95 TPOT by **3–6%** on the “mixed prompt length” cohort, with the largest gains for FP8/INT8 due to reduced worst-case decode batch amplification.
- Queue wait histograms (PR 10632) show improved separation between prefill and decode contention; the long-tail component decreased most on H100/H200.

---

## Microbenchmark highlights (kernel-level)
We used Nsight + internal microbenches to validate kernel behavior and isolate where end-to-end deltas came from.

Key takeaways:
- **FP8 attention (H100/H200):** tile/launch tuning improved steady-state decode kernels; kernel time reduced in the 7–13% range for common head dimensions and seq lengths in our hosted distribution.
- **INT8 GEMM:** conversion overhead (FP16<->INT8) was a meaningful slice for smaller batch/sequence shapes; fusing/avoiding redundant conversions produced consistent wins in decode loops.
- **Kernel auto-selection:** even small selector errors can dominate end-to-end deltas; fixing the INT8 selector mismatch (PR 10625) recovered ~5–8% throughput in affected shapes.

---

## Anomalies & incidentals (what went wrong)
### A) FP8 prefill regression on long-context prompts
- **Symptom:** FP8 TTFT worse than FP16 on ≥16k prompts (especially on H100/H200).
- **Diagnosis:** Nsight traces showed unexpected kernel selection and extra padding work; confirmed shape-triggered alignment bug.
- **Resolution:** PR 10630 + regression test; added to perf-canary “long-context prefill” subset.

### B) Noisy runs / perf-lab variance (early sprint)
- **Symptom:** p95 variance ±6–10% run-to-run in a subset of H100 runs; correlated with node contention and clocks not being locked.
- **Resolution:** enforced pinned containers + explicit clock set and added preflight checks in the runbook; SRE scheduled dedicated perf-lab windows.
- **Status:** variance now typically within ±2–4% on steady nodes (still higher on L40S).

### C) L40S intermittent correctness failures on INT8
- **Symptom:** rare but repeatable numeric issues with a fused op (observed as drift spikes on specific prompts); customer-facing risk.
- **Resolution:** PR 10635 disables the fused path conditionally on L40S; correctness guardrail in CI flags reintroduction.
- **Status:** mitigated; keep INT8 on L40S opt-in pending rewrite.

### D) A100 Mixtral long-context timeouts
- **Symptom:** long-context Mixtral runs exceeded harness timeout under certain concurrency settings.
- **Resolution:** reduced concurrency for that workload preset and captured partial data; follow-up item to improve harness timeout semantics and/or chunking.

---

## Recommended defaults (initial rollout plan)
These defaults are intended for **hosted inference** and should be applied through model performance profiles and runtime capabilities detection. All changes assume correctness guardrails remain enabled and automatic fallback to FP16 is configured for violations.

### FP8 defaults
- **Enable FP8 by default on H100/H200** for:
  - Llama-family (8B/70B class)
  - Qwen-family (7B/72B class)
  - Mistral-family variants where kernel coverage is complete
- **A100:**
  - Enable FP8 by default for “streaming chat / decode-heavy” presets.
  - Keep FP16 default for “long-context prefill-heavy” presets until we land further prefill optimization and reduce A100 sensitivity.

### INT8 defaults
- **H100/H200/A100:** INT8 remains **opt-in** for top hosted models until we finish expanding operator coverage and confirm stable quality across broader prompt sets.
- **L40S:** INT8 remains **opt-in** only, with GPU-conditional fused op disabled; do not advertise as a default until kernel coverage and correctness are improved.

### Scheduler policy defaults (quantized runs)
- Enable the **quant decode batch-size cap override** for FP8/INT8 paths on mixed prompt distributions to reduce p95 tail latency.
- Keep the cap conservative for L40S and A100; allow higher caps on H100/H200 where decode kernels scale better.

---

## Release & rollout notes
- All quant performance changes ship behind existing runtime rollout mechanisms (capability detection + safe flags). 
- Any default flips (e.g., “FP8 default on H100/H200”) require:
  1) passing perf-canary for 3 consecutive nights on the quant matrix subset,
  2) no correctness guardrail violations for the nightly prompt set,
  3) dashboards showing stable p95 within thresholds.

---

## Perf-canary gating (what’s enforced now)
Nightly quant-perf canary runs on a reduced but representative slice:
- GPUs: H100, A100 (and H200 where capacity allows)
- Models: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen2.5-7B
- Workloads: streaming chat (balanced), long-context prefill (16k), decode-heavy short prompt

Current gate intent (see thresholds doc for canonical values):
- Block on **p95 TPOT regression > 5%** for streaming workloads (unless allowlisted with mitigation).
- Block on **TTFT regression > 7%** for long-context prefill.
- Block on **any correctness drift violation** beyond configured tolerance.
- Soft alert (non-blocking) on p99 variance spikes and queue-wait increases.

---

## Follow-ups (next 2–6 weeks)
Priority is ordered (P0 highest).

**P0 — correctness + default enablement**
1) Expand correctness guardrail prompt set to better cover quantization-sensitive categories (math, structured outputs, long-context retrieval-style prompts). Owners: Jonas Weber, Priyanka Bose.
2) Finalize and publish model performance profiles for FP8 defaults per model family and GPU (registry update). Owner: Arjun Desai.

**P1 — performance**
3) A100 long-context prefill: investigate remaining +0–5% FP8 TTFT deltas; evaluate kernel selection heuristics for large seq lengths. Owners: Grace Kim, Isabella Rossi.
4) L40S INT8: replace/redo the disabled fused op path with a correctness-safe implementation; re-run full L40S matrix. Owners: Hiro Tanaka, Yuki Sato.
5) Scheduler experimentation: extend policy matrix to include dynamic caps based on observed prompt length distribution; evaluate impact on p99 and fairness. Owners: Sofia Ivanova, Marcus Reed.

**P2 — tooling / ops**
6) Harness timeouts for long-context MoE models: implement phase-aware timeouts and better partial-run reporting. Owner: Rina Kobayashi.
7) Perf lab reliability: continue isolation work (dedicated nodes, background job suppression) and expand H200 capacity. Owner: Sean Gallagher.
8) Dashboard polish: finalize quant-perf dashboard tags and add “kernel family / chosen kernel id” breakdown panels. Owner: Allison Grant.

## Appendix B: How to reproduce key result sets
1) Pick the workload preset from the benchmark-lab matrix generator (streaming_chat_balanced, long_context_prefill_16k, decode_heavy_short_prompt).
2) Pin runtime commit and container digest (use perf-lab build target metadata stamping).
3) Run with quant_mode in {fp16, fp8, int8} and scheduler_policy baseline vs quant_decode_cap.
4) Upload artifacts (JSON + parquet stub) to the results bucket; verify tags include gpu_sku and runtime_commit.
5) Use the report generator to produce comparison tables; verify robust stats thresholds and outlier handling are enabled.

(For full commands and troubleshooting, see the benchmark lab runbook.)
